items.title: Friday, November 20, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content: When the Fujifilm X100VI was first announced, I preordered one that day. After waiting 6 months for one to become available, I canceled the order and moved on. That was more than two years ago, and I still want one. They are still difficult to find at retail prices, but I got a notification this morning that a black one was in stock at B&H so I dropped everything and hit that "Add to Cart" button as quickly as I could. It shipped this afternoon and will be here by Tuesday. I'll hang on to the Q2 for now, but the idea is that the Fuji will take over for the Leica as a carry-everwhere camera. It's better suited to it.

items.title: Faking contact sheets with an app
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
I don't enjoy making contact sheets in the darkroom, but I love them, so Claude and I made an app for it.

I've tried printing "Contact sheets" from apps like Lightroom, etc. but they don't look at all like contact sheets. They're just a boring grid. I wanted something nicer.

I know, it's cheating, but in just a couple of hours I had a native macOS app that generates JPG or PDF contact sheets from a collection of film scans. I drag the scans onto the app, enter the roll number, camera, film stock, date, and any notes about the roll and I get a reasonable facsimile of a real contact sheet.

I print them on US Letter sized photo paper. There's room on the left to punch holes for the ring binder. Stack them above the matching negative sleeve and it's almost like the real thing, without the hassle.

I wish I had the energy to make actual contact sheets in the darkroom, but I don't. I'll take this instead.
